title: Notification Policy Simulation Playground — wireframes & grooming notes
content:
Purpose:
A lightweight working doc for a Notification Policy Simulation feature in the Console. Goal is to let PM/engineers/designers prototype how policies (channels, thresholds, suppression windows, tenant defaults) behave against historical signal and a synthetic traffic generator before we ship rollout controls.

Problem statement:
- Users currently tweak alert rules and only discover noisy/faulty policies in prod after oncall fatigue.
- Changes to channel fanout and thresholding are hard to reason about across multi-tenant orgs.
- We need a way to preview and simulate outcomes (recipient counts, estimated monthly notification volume, expected SLA breach events) before committing policy changes.

Core UX ideas (high level):
1) Simulation Sandbox workspace (left column): select a target scope (global tenant defaults | product route | specific service) and pick a time window (historic replay) or synthetic traffic profile.
2) Policy Builder (center pane): drag/drop policy layers. Each layer shows: name, precedence, channels (email/slack/pager/sms/webhook), threshold config, suppression windows, escalation rules. Editable inline.
3) Quick Feedback (right rail): immediate simulation summary: estimated notifies, estimated monthly cost (tokens + channel cost proxy), noisy-risk score, top impacted recipients, example notifications.
4) Live preview: expandable notification card that renders final formatted payload for each channel. Support function call examples and rate-limited streaming preview.

Wireframe notes (quick sketches translated to text):
- Top toolbar: Scope dropdown | Mode: replay vs synthetic | Run Simulation (big blue) | Save as Draft | Compare (A/B)
- Left column: Scope tree (All tenants > Org > Project > Route) with checkboxes for multi-select. Quick 'pick last 7d' or 'custom range' date selector under tree.
- Center: Policy timeline canvas. Layers stacked: Tenant default (grey, locked) -> Product override -> Route-specific rule (blue). Each layer card: header (name, precedence badge), channel pills (icons), threshold summary (e.g. 3 alerts / 5m), mute icon, edit chevron. Click opens inline editor drawer.
- Inline editor drawer: toggles for channel enable, numeric threshold sliders, cron-style suppression windows, escalation steps (1 -> 2 -> fallback). Preview CTA at bottom: 'Run preview for this layer'.
- Right rail: Simulation summary cards:
  * Total expected notifications: 1,892
  * Estimated recipients: 124 unique endpoints
  * Cost estimate: $74/month (channels + infra proxy)
  * Noisy-risk: High (75%)
  * Top 5 recipients (email/slack/pager) with counts
  * Toggle to view detailed replay timeline (expandable)

Simulation behavior & constraints to model:
- De-dup window: 60s default, per-channel override. Dedup should reduce repeated notifications for same incident across channels by default.
- Merge similar signals: fuzzy-keying based on route + fingerprint fields.
- Backoff/escalation simulation: simulate escalation when primary channel not acknowledged in X minutes (simulate ack probabilities).
- Quota & throttling: simulate tenant-level daily caps and route burst protection.
- Multitenancy: when scope = org, show per-project breakdown and aggregated totals.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Users can select a scope and time window and run a simulation against historical events (7d).
- Policy Builder supports adding/removing channels and editing thresholds for at least two layers.
- Simulation summarizes: notification count, unique recipients, and a cost estimate.
- Live preview renders the final notification payload for at least email and slack channels.
- Save as Draft stores policy changes without applying to live routing (backend flag).

Grooming backlog (initial tickets & rough T-shirt sizing):
- SIM-101: backend simulator API that replays 7d of events with fingerprinting and dedupe (L/2)
- SIM-102: policy layer model + precedence rules (M/3)
- SIM-103: center canvas wireframe + inline editor (S/2)
- SIM-104: right rail simulation summary UI + cost estimator (M/3)
- SIM-105: live notification preview renderer (email/slack) (S/1)
- SIM-106: synthetic traffic generator (configurable flood/spike/steady) (M/3)
- SIM-107: A/B compare diff view for two policies (L/5)
- SIM-108: multi-tenant aggregation UI (M/3)
- SIM-109: e2e QA plan + replay fixtures (S/2)

Edge cases & open questions (notes to triage):
- How to represent costs accurately? Start with a proxy cost-per-notify by channel and attach token-cost for infra; escalate later to real billing integration.
- Permissions model: who can run simulations? who can save drafts? Ensure role gating for enterprise tenants.
- Replay fidelity: are we comfortable replaying PII-bearing payloads into a simulation? Likely need anonymization or toggle.
- Failure modes: simulator should return quick failure reasons (missing events, insufficient retention) and not block console.
- Complexity of suppression windows UI: consider natural-language presets (e.g., "quiet nights 22:00-07:00 local") vs cron editor.

Prototype interactions (user flows):
1) PM picks 'Org' scope, range = last 7d. Starts with Tenant default policy visible. Adds a Route-specific layer, enables pager and slack, sets threshold 5 alerts / 1m. Runs simulation. Sees noisy-risk drop from 86% to 42%. Saves draft and assigns to SRE for review (links to JIRA).
2) SRE runs A/B compare between current live policy and draft. Uses 'replay only failed incidents' filter to validate that false positives were handled. Approves -> policy saved as rollout.

Design constraints and priorities (for grooming):
- MVP must not attempt to model exact billing. Use proxy numbers.
- UI should be keyboard-accessible and allow JSON export/import of policy layers.
- Keep scope selection performant (lazy load tenant trees).
- Keep simulation run async with progress and cancellable.

Next steps (short term):
- Design: produce 3 low-fi screens for the canvas, inline editor, and right rail (Zoe) — due 2025-02-20.
- Backend: prototype replay API + dedupe (Marco) — spike complete 2025-02-28.
- PM: draft acceptance criteria + initial tickets (Asha) — create JIRA by 2025-02-14.

Notes to reviewers:
- Focus feedback on developer experience for writing custom suppression rules and on how the cost proxy should surface.
- We intentionally defer bundling with the full Rollouts UI for now to reduce scope.

References & links:
- Related: CONFLUENCE-UI-4872 (policy precedence doc)
- Example incident replay fixtures: s3://redwood-test-fixtures/sim/replay/2025-01
- Prior art: PagerDuty notification rules + OpsGenie simulation MVP notes

Scratchpad (raw brainstorm snippets):
- "preview: show raw body, parsed templated fields, link to function call logs"
- "cost slider: tradeoff noise vs coverage"
- "toggle: show which policy layer actually suppressed each notification (traceable)"
- "export: generate terraform/json for policy that can be provisioned via private deployments"
- "UX microcopy: when simulation shows >10k notifies, show big red banner 'High risk: might exceed tenant daily cap'"

-- end of doc --
